title: Pipedream Free Plan: Limits and Alternatives (2026)
summary: Pipedream free plan provides metered credits before workflows pause. See how it stacks up against six alternative automation tools with free options.
body_markdown:
## Rebuilding the workflow in Activepieces and where its free tier falls short


If you want an open-source tool you can self-host for nothing, with a paid cloud plan as the fallback, Activepieces covers both: its core is MIT-licensed and runs on your own server with no licence fee, and the same flows run on its managed cloud when you'd rather not watch a server.


Its free cloud tier is metered in credits, so the same night-time cliff applies. The alert still goes on first.


### What the rebuild looked like


I rebuilt a support-ticket flow: a HubSpot trigger, one of the 750 integrations counted in the open source monorepo, fires when a ticket is created, two AI steps rewrite and categorize it, a Router (Activepieces' name for a branching step) splits it by category, so each category of ticket now gets its own processing path.


Each branch posts to Slack.


In the screenshot below, the finished canvas shows the "New Ticket Added" trigger on the right with its Connection field, three branches (Branch 1, Branch 2, Otherwise), and Test Flow active before Publish.


Take from it that the Otherwise branch is the one that catches everything unexpected, so a ticket never vanishes silently. It took one sitting, not a weekend.


The[Activepieces pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) states 1 credit per flow run, whatever the number of steps, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module. So this ticket flow with its router and Slack branches costs the same per run as a two-step version.


The two AI steps are the exception, at 2 credits each for a fast model. Test runs count too, which means building and debugging spends part of the month's allowance before a real ticket arrives.


### Where the free tier falls short


The[Activepieces pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) lists three cloud tiers by credit allowance, so users choose based on expected volume.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) says Free is $0 per month for 1,000 credits, which suits a prototype or a quiet inbox, so you won't outgrow this tier for these use cases.


It doesn't suit a team that sees a few hundred tickets a week once each run uses several credits.


Plus is $20 per month for 10,000 credits, ten times the allowance for $20, so this is the sensible first upgrade.


Activepieces' Team plan is $200 per month for 50,000 credits, which is five times the Plus allowance at ten times the price, meaning each credit costs roughly twice as much at this tier.


It only makes sense if you need what else that plan adds, not just volume.


### Is the free cloud tier safe for critical workflows?


Credit caps are only part of it. I wouldn't call the free cloud tier a safe home for a business-critical flow, because the metered limit is exactly where an unwatched flow stops.


The free tier also leaves out what sits behind paid plans: SSO arrives with Team, while SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, secret managers and releases with Git Sync belong to Ultimate.


To go the bootstrap route, self-host the open-source edition, which removes the credit meter but moves the risk to you. You own upgrades, backups and uptime, so a server that falls over at 2 a.m. is your problem, not a vendor's.


Choose it only if someone on your team will actually watch the server. If nobody will, stay on cloud, set the alert, and pay the $20 when the alert fires.
